extracted.intended_audience: researchers, engineers, program managers, and proposers preparing high-risk research and technology project proposals for funding reviewers (e.g., DARPA-style evaluations)
extracted.subtask_description: A concise eight-question framework for framing and evaluating high-risk, high-payoff research and technology projects; used to structure proposal narratives and reviewer assessments of objectives, novelty, risks, cost, schedule, and success metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are you trying to do? Articulate your objectives using absolutely no jargon.
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state the project's objectives in plain language, avoiding technical jargon so non-specialists can understand the intended outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use absolutely no jargon; succinctly convey the core goal and what the project will accomplish.

rubrics_metrics.name: How is it done today, and what are the limits of current practice?
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the current state-of-the-art or prevailing approaches and explicitly identify their limitations or why they are inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain existing solutions/practices and the specific performance, capability, cost, scale, or other limits that motivate the new work.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is new in your approach and why do you think it will be successful?
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate the novel aspects of the proposed approach and provide the rationale or evidence for why these innovations are likely to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight what differentiates the approach from current practice and the technical or conceptual reasons supporting its feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who cares? If you are successful, what difference will it make?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the significance, beneficiaries, and impact of success—who will use or benefit from the results and what change will occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address practical, societal, military, commercial, or scientific value and the scale of the anticipated difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are the risks?
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify key technical, programmatic, and other risks that could prevent successful outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about uncertainties, assumptions, potential failure modes, and critical unknowns that must be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much will it cost?
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an estimate of the resources and budget required to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State expected costs (funding, personnel, equipment, operations) and justify the estimate relative to scope and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: How long will it take?
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a timeline for the project, including duration and major schedule milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present realistic schedule estimates tied to tasks and risk mitigation; indicate key phases and expected time-to-results.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are the mid-term and final "exams" to check for success?
rubrics_metrics.description: Define measurable interim and final milestones, tests, or metrics that will be used to evaluate progress and determine success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify concrete, observable criteria (experiments, demonstrations, performance thresholds) for mid-term assessments and final acceptance.
